summary: Gaeng hang lay (also called hang le) is a slow-braised northern Thai pork curry with a dark, savoury-sweet spice and tamarind character, usually served with rice. For a focused tasting, order Hung Lay Moo at Kiti Panit, a Northern Thai restaurant in an old Tha Phae Road mansion; its current menu lists the curry at ฿390. Gaj Kitchen and Bar lists another version for ฿280 before service and tax.
whyGo: A rich, aromatic northern curry with a distinct ginger, spice and tamarind profile; Michelin describes Kiti Panit's version as intense and complex.
It is an easy dish to share with rice and other Lanna plates, or order as the main reason for a meal.
bestFor: Travellers interested in regional northern Thai food and slow-cooked pork.
Groups who want to share several northern dishes in a historic setting.
skipIf: You avoid pork or need a vegetarian, vegan or halal meal; the featured versions are pork curry.
You have a serious peanut or other food allergy and cannot confirm ingredients and cross-contact directly with the restaurant.
duration: Allow 60–90 minutes for a sit-down meal; planning estimate, and queues may extend this.
cost: Kiti Panit's current online menu lists Hung Lay Moo at ฿390. Gaj lists Gang Hung Lay at ฿280, with 10% service charge and applicable 7% tax added. Rice, drinks and other dishes cost extra.
hours: Kiti Panit says it is open Wednesday–Monday, 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–22:00 (last order 21:30), closed Tuesday. Gaj lists all-day dining 11:30–23:00. Recheck close to the visit.
bestTime: Lunch or early dinner; verify the chosen restaurant's schedule and allow time for a shared meal.
gettingThere: Kiti Panit is at 19 Tha Phae Road in the Old City/Chang Khlan area. The Japan National Tourism Organization's Kiti Panit listing says it is about a 10-minute walk from Tha Phae Gate. For a longer cross-town trip, use a taxi or ride-hail to the restaurant address; exact fares and current transit routes were not verified. Gaj is on Chang Klan Road; use its current map pin for a direct ride.
booking: Kiti Panit asks guests to book directly; call +66 80 191 7996 or use its website's booking/order links. Michelin also says the restaurant manages its own bookings. Gaj's booking arrangements were not verified here.
accessibility: Step-free access, accessible toilets, and mobility access inside Kiti Panit's historic mansion were not verified. Contact the restaurant before visiting if these affect your plans; Gaj accessibility details were also not established.
practicalTips: Ask for gaeng hang lay or hang le (แกงฮังเล); the Kiti Panit menu calls its dish Hung Lay Moo and describes it as northern pork curry.
The dish is meat-based and commonly includes pork, ginger, peanuts and a spice paste; recipes vary. Ask staff about peanuts, fish sauce, shrimp paste and cross-contact if relevant.
Consider sharing one portion with rice and ordering vegetables or other dishes alongside it; the curry is rich.

Kiti Panit's website and Michelin currently differ on its weekly schedule: the restaurant says closed Tuesday, while Michelin lists Tuesday closed as well but the Japanese tourism listing says daily. Follow the restaurant's own current schedule and reconfirm around holidays.
decemberNotes: This is an everyday menu dish, not a seasonal event. December brings busy travel dates and Christmas/New Year schedule changes may apply; reserve directly and reconfirm opening hours, menu and price shortly before your meal.
uncertainties: The restaurant's online menu and listed price may change before December 2026; no date-specific menu was found.
Transit fares, step-free access, allergy protocols and holiday opening hours were not confirmed.
The Commons photo is an older representative bowl photographed in Chiang Mai, not a current serving at either named venue.
